clue.text: Entering shopping centre, both bananas put aside for later use

indicators.note: the scrambled letters go into the middle of the shopping-centre word, so entering signals insertion

parts.note: a mall is a shopping centre

indicators.note: going bananas means going crazy, so these letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: Two bananas are tucked away in a shopping centre to be eaten later.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bananas' looks like fruit going into storage, but it means crazy and scrambles the word before it.
explanation.definitionFit: Something mothballed is stored away unused, kept in reserve for a later date.

clue.text: Run when philanderer turns up

indicators.note: in a down clue, turning up means the word is read from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: a wolf is a predatory womaniser

explanation.surface: Someone runs off just as the womaniser shows his face.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turns up' looks like 'arrives' but reverses WOLF in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms as verbs: water runs or streams along its course.

clue.text: Dog in the evening sun, perhaps?

definitions.meaning: a red or English ... is a breed of gun dog
the sun goes down in the evening, so it is something that sets; the question mark marks the sun as one example

explanation.surface: A dog basks in the last of the evening sunshine.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading is whimsical: anything that sets could be called by this word, and the sun at dusk does.
explanation.definitionFit: A gun-dog breed name, and a playful noun for anything that goes down below the horizon.

clue.text: Case of puppy, 3, as the best thing with the cat?

definitions.text: the best thing with the cat?

indicators.note: the case of a word is its outer shell, so only its first and last letters are kept

parts.note: 3 down is a setter, and jam is something that sets as it cools
taken as written

explanation.surface: A puppy and a setter compete with the cat for top place.
explanation.walkthrough: '3' points to the answer of 3 down, SETTER, read as a thing that sets: JAM. 'The cat's pyjamas' is slang for the very best.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom 'the cat's pyjamas' means something excellent, so these garments go with the cat to mean the best.

clue.text: See 24
Old singer saves half of soup for dog

indicators.note: to save something is to keep it safe within, so the singer's name holds the soup fragment

parts.note: Kathleen Ferrier was an English contralto who died in 1953

indicators.note: only the first three of the six letters of the soup survive

parts.note: oxtail is a classic British soup

explanation.surface: A veteran vocalist puts aside half a bowl of soup for the dog.
explanation.walkthrough: The old singer is Kathleen Ferrier, a famous English contralto of the 1940s; the soup is oxtail, a British staple.
explanation.definitionFit: A breed example: this small terrier was bred for bolting foxes from their earths.

clue.text: State, I'm sorry to say, kicked around for starters

parts.note: alas is an exclamation of regret

indicators.note: starters are the opening letters of the following words

explanation.surface: An apologetic admission that someone was kicked around at the beginning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'State' looks like a verb (to say) but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the largest of the fifty US states, bought from Russia in 1867.

clue.text: Fanciful art of sheepdog training is mine?

definitions.meaning: a made-up skill on the pattern of falconry: the craft of working collies
a coal mine with its buildings and workings

explanation.surface: Someone claims the whimsical craft of training sheepdogs as their own.
explanation.walkthrough: The first reading invents a word like falconry from the breed name; it can also be seen as COLLIE plus RY (railway, a 'training' line).
explanation.definitionFit: A coal pit, together with its surface buildings, is called by this name in Britain.

clue.text: Trick after a backflip nailed by European dog

indicators.note: something nailed by another is held fast inside it here, so the reversed piece sits within

parts.note: a Pole is a European, from Poland

indicators.note: a backflip turns the word over, so it is read backwards

parts.note: to do someone is to cheat or trick them

explanation.surface: An acrobatic trick from a European with a performing dog.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trick' reads as a noun beside the backflip, but it is the verb 'do', as in to cheat someone.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a curly-coated breed, the classic show dog.

clue.text: Meals for a dog

definitions.meaning: slang for food or a meal
the ... ... is a Chinese breed with a blue-black tongue

explanation.definitionFit: Slang for grub, and a short name for a fluffy Chinese dog breed.

clue.text: Extraordinary stature, I am in shock

indicators.note: something extraordinary is out of the ordinary, so these letters break their usual order

explanation.surface: Someone admits being stunned by another's remarkable height.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Extraordinary' looks like a description of stature but signals rearranging STATURE plus IAM.
explanation.definitionFit: A verb synonym: to cause deep emotional distress or upset.

clue.text: Cat, a killer losing tail in conflict

indicators.note: the pieces sit inside the conflict word, signalled by in

parts.note: a jar is an old word for a quarrel or clash

indicators.note: the weapon drops its final letter

parts.note: a gun is a killing weapon

explanation.surface: A deadly cat suffers an injury to its tail in a fight.
explanation.walkthrough: A plus GU (GUN 'losing tail') goes 'in' JAR, an old word for a quarrel.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the big spotted cat of Central and South America.

clue.text: Top dog unsurprisingly stealing spectacles, misbehaving

definitions.text: Top dog unsurprisingly stealing spectacles, misbehaving

indicators.note: the thief takes the goods into itself, so the scrambled letters close around the spectacles
letters that misbehave will not stay in line, so they are thrown into a new order

parts.note: only the opening syllable of this word is taken, the two letters before surprisingly
two round lenses look like a pair of O's

explanation.surface: The leader of the pack, predictably, makes off with someone's glasses and causes mischief.
explanation.walkthrough: Paul splits 'unsurprisingly' as UN + 'surprisingly', the leading UN joining 'Top dog' as anagram fodder; the whole clue also pictures a dog causing trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes someone engaged in mischief or plotting something bad, as a thieving dog is.

clue.text: Opera in a borstal extremely unusual

indicators.note: the opera sits within the other letters, signalled by in
the extremes of a word are its first and last letters

parts.note: Norma is Bellini's opera

explanation.surface: Staging an opera in a youth detention centre would be very odd.
explanation.walkthrough: A borstal was a British prison for young offenders; Norma is Bellini's tragic opera.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: deviating from what is normal or usual.

clue.text: A junior officer in green, unsurpassed

indicators.note: the officer is placed inside the colour word

parts.note: lime is a shade of green
Lt is the abbreviation for lieutenant

explanation.surface: A young officer, still green, proves unbeatable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Green' looks like 'inexperienced', but it is the colour LIME.
explanation.definitionFit: As in an all-time high: a record never beaten across the whole of history.

clue.text: Cat literarily a degree above hole

indicators.note: in a down clue, the first piece sits above the second

parts.note: an MA is a Master of Arts degree
a cavity is a hollow or hole

explanation.surface: A cat with academic credentials climbs above a hole.
explanation.walkthrough: The mystery cat of T. S. Eliot's Old Possum's Book of Practical Cats is the literary feline.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: Eliot's 'Mystery Cat', the master criminal of his poems.

clue.text: Dutch painter capturing cat in a neat way

indicators.note: the painter holds the cat inside his name

parts.note: Sir Peter Lely was a Dutch-born portrait painter
a gib is a castrated tomcat

explanation.surface: A Dutch artist catches a cat on canvas with tidy precision.
explanation.walkthrough: A gib is an old dialect word for a tomcat; Lely was court painter to Charles II.
explanation.definitionFit: Neat handwriting can be read easily, so writing neatly is writing readably.

clue.text: Cat drops on cat as a means of survival

indicators.note: the big cat lets go of the letters of on

parts.note: a lion is a big cat
taken as written
a feline is any member of the cat family

explanation.surface: One cat landing on another to stay alive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drops on' looks like 'lands on' but removes ON from LION, leaving LI.
explanation.definitionFit: Figuratively, a rope or resource that keeps someone afloat and alive.

clue.text: Dog hugging Rover, totally gutted in sounding like a cat

indicators.note: the dog wraps itself around the other letters

parts.note: a pug is a small snub-nosed breed

indicators.note: with all its insides removed, only the outer letters remain

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A dog cuddles Rover, who is utterly heartbroken, and makes a cat's noise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Totally gutted' looks like 'devastated' but empties ROVER to RR.
explanation.definitionFit: Making the low contented vibrating sound a cat makes.

clue.text: Fine wine, relative filth finally coming first

parts.note: gran is a grandmother

indicators.note: the last letter of the filth word moves round to its front

parts.note: crud is dirt or grime

explanation.surface: Grandma's dirt somehow ends up first in line for a fine vintage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Finally coming first' moves the D of CRUD to the front, DCRU.
explanation.definitionFit: French for 'great growth', the top classification of a vineyard or its wine.

clue.text: Fruit is eaten by cats and dogs, perhaps?

indicators.note: what is eaten goes inside the eater

parts.note: it can rain cats and dogs, so these stand for a heavy downpour

explanation.surface: A pet asks whether cats and dogs will eat the fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cats and dogs' wants to mean pets, but it is rain, as in the idiom 'raining cats and dogs'.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a dried grape is a kind of fruit.

clue.text: Something felt to protect female suffering loss

indicators.note: the hat surrounds and shields the letter

parts.note: a beret is a soft hat made of felt

explanation.surface: A woman feels deep grief and needs protection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Something felt' reads as an emotion, but it is a hat made of felt.
explanation.definitionFit: Deprived of something, especially grieving the death of a loved one.

clue.text: Keeping dry, fragment split in half

indicators.note: the fragment holds the dry word within it

parts.note: a bit is a small piece
sec is the French wine term for dry

explanation.surface: A dried fragment breaks into two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: To cut into two equal parts, a geometry term.

clue.text: Girl running round borders in garden to catch some balls, runs the wrong way

indicators.note: the girl's title goes all the way round the rest

parts.note: miss is a girl or young unmarried woman

indicators.note: the border letters close around the cricket balls
the borders of a word are its first and last letters

parts.note: an over in cricket is a set of six balls

explanation.surface: A girl dashes about the garden fielding cricket balls.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket an over is six balls. 'Runs' in the definition means governs or manages.
explanation.definitionFit: To govern or manage a country or organisation badly.

clue.text: Large cutting tool's shaft

indicators.note: the letter cuts into the tool word, sitting inside it

parts.note: an axe is a chopping tool
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: A big chopping tool has a long handle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cutting tool' looks like one phrase, but 'cutting' is the insertion signal and 'tool' is AXE.
explanation.definitionFit: A rod on which wheels turn, a kind of shaft.

clue.text: Cat partial to nastiest sort of drink

indicators.note: read as part-way into, so the cat sits partway along the scrambled letters
to sort is to rearrange, so these letters are put into a new order

parts.note: a puma is a big American cat

explanation.surface: A cat with a fondness for the nastiest kind of drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Partial to' looks like 'fond of' but means part-way into: the cat goes inside ASTISNTE, the rearranged letters from 'sort of'.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a sweet sparkling Italian wine from Piedmont.

clue.text: Eat a lot — good taste!

parts.note: pi is short for pious, morally good
gout is French for taste

explanation.surface: Eating heartily is a sign of good taste.
explanation.walkthrough: GOUT is the French word for taste, borrowed into English.
explanation.definitionFit: An informal phrasal verb for gorging or eating greedily.

clue.text: Poisonous compound not designed to impress one in particular

indicators.note: the scrambled group sits inside the word for particular

parts.note: nice can mean fussy or particular, as in a nice distinction

indicators.note: to impress is to press something in, so the letter goes into the scrambled ones
letters designed anew are arranged into a different pattern

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A poison was not made just to impress any single person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Designed' rearranges the word not as OTN, and 'to impress' presses the one inside that, before it all goes into the word for particular.
explanation.definitionFit: The toxic alkaloid found in tobacco is a poisonous chemical compound.
